reviews.text:
Awful place. We’ve used many vets and it’s the only one that our dog was scared to be at visibly.
Their reception takes forever to reach out to by phone, they have no problem with making you wait does doctor for half an hour when you are 10 min late be wise there’s no parking in the vicinity, they strictly adhere to the show-on-time policy. For a strange reason they wouldn’t allow you to be with your dog during vaccination, ours was visibly shaken when brought out of the exam room.
All that combined with lack of parking, generally dirty and disgusting outside street - the decision to switch to another vet was easy.
Avoid!

I had an appt for my dog with Christy Silvaberg today and had a terrible experience. They don't care about your dog's health and are more concerned about making money. I have a 2 year old bernedoodle and needed more flea/tick meds which I ordered from Chewy. This vet office denied the request and said i had to bring him in for a general exam (which was $100 and all she did was listen to his heartbeat and spent maybe 90 seconds with him). Then required a heartworm test which was another $85. But this wasn't even the worst part. Christy Silvaberg walked in the exam room and the first thing she asked was "do you not believe in vaccines?" Which I responded and said that I only get the necessary vaccines for my dog - aka the rabies - and denied the others. Which then she asked me "did you get the COVID vaccine" and when I responded to her she gave me the most judgemental look which was so unprofessional. First, it's completely inappropriate to ask a client a personal medical question when it has absolutely nothing to do with the pet. Second, her reaction to my response was extremely rude and unprofessional.

Do yourself a favor and find somewhere else to go. From the reception, to the vet tech, to the vets themselves...they were all rude, start to finish. DO NOT GO HERE!

I cannot say enough positive about Sunset Cliffs Animal Hospital. Everyone is wonderful but my vet, Dr. Whitted, has been absolutely outstanding. My dog has had 2 emergency surgeries since we moved back to San Diego 4 months ago. Dr Whitted has kindly and patiently worked with me to figure out what’s wrong. She is so smart and sweet that she makes what could be a stressful experience a pleasure. Highly recommend.
The front desk staff is so incompetent and I was really concerned with the technicians when the pet went inside I'm wondering if they did what they were supposed to do!

We recently joined Sunset Cliffs Animal Hospital and had such a great experience with Willow’s physical, vaccines, and teeth cleaning. She did amazing, and the staff was wonderful from the front desk to the back office team. Everyone was kind, caring, and made both Willow and me feel comfortable throughout the entire process. So thankful to have found such a great veterinary team for Willow!

Dr. Silvaberg is the best Veterinarian! We drive from Encinitas for her to treat our French Bulldog and Bulldog boxer mix. She is so calm, kind, knowledgeable and encouraging in every situation. Our dogs have thrived in her care.
They actually care and are very responsive. Highly recommend.
Jenna Whitted, DVM was absolutely amazing. All the staff was wonderful.
Thank you so much for your 5-star review! We truly appreciate your support and are grateful for the opportunity to care for your pets. We look forward to seeing Maggie and Stitch soon!

Wonderful vet! Everyone is so kind here. We're new, and the face us a warm welcome. I trusted them to nueter our puppy Oscar, and they did a fantastic job. He's doing well. Highly recommend Sunset Cliffs Animal Hospital. 10/10

I brought my English bulldog mix to see Dr. Silvberg for the first time after a frustrating experience with another vet and specifically wanted a doctor familiar with the breed. The previous vet ran X-rays and blood work, couldn’t find a cause for what I thought was a seizure, yet still prescribed epilepsy medication, which I wasn’t comfortable putting my dog on for life without a clear diagnosis. Dr. Silvberg took the time to truly listen, explained that she didn't think my dog had a seizure, and advised against the medication—something that could have actually caused seizures if he were ever taken off it. She was incredibly patient, never made me feel dismissed or like a bad pet owner, and even sat on the floor with my dog to really get to know him. She was far more knowledgeable about English bulldogs and offered insight into other possible causes based on common breed-related health issues. Her staff was also amazing and brought out water and a fan since my dog overheats easily when excited. - I would say the visit was a bit pricey, but was absolutely worth it, especially after spending $900 at a previous vet for incorrect information. I highly recommend this facility, and especially Dr. Silvberg. My little man will only be seeing her from now on.

Great veterinarian (Dr Silva-berg) we always have a good experience there. Today we adopted our foster English Bulldog from Rescue love bulldogs. Allesendra is wonderful to work with, Roxy is our second rescue from her, Grandpa Moke was our first and he was so sweet. We're looking forward to many years with Roxy.

They’ve tried multiple attempts to collect on a fake charge. I took my cat in 6 months ago and received an invoice for $30 via email. No explanation of what the charges were for or anything. I sent several emails asking what the charge was for and then they told me it was for a nail trim. Funny because no nail trim was ever done during the visit since my cat was with me the entire time. And if it did happen, why are you now charging me six months later? Several additional emails later, they are now, claiming that it was for one of my other cats who I have never brought in to this clinic. This is truly sad how much they are reaching just to collect some extra funds from customers. Because we had a very good visit when I brought mochi in, and the staff was extremely friendly.

I’ve been coming to this veterinary hospital for years! Dr. Whitted and Dr. Silvaberg have such knowledge when it comes to my bulldog Kaira. ♥️. I trust their opinions 100%
And shout out to Bren for the kindness and knowledge when it came to the meds my girl needed ..
Thank you all for such smooth visits every time.

I’ve been bringing my dogs here since 2016, and they’ve cared for four of them over the years. Ranging from my big, gentle Bernese Mountain Dogs to energetic Pitty mixes and even my little Shih Tzu mix. The whole team is warm, kind, knowledgeable, and always gets us in quickly. They explain every option clearly and never push unnecessary treatments. They just provide genuine care. They treat my pets like their own, and I wouldn’t trust anyone else in San Diego.
We LOVE Dr. Silvaberg and staff!!! We have been seeing her for over 20 years! We trust her with our dogs and know she will do what's best for them!
THE BEST veterinary clinic in San Diego; They have taken excellent care of my boy since he was a tiny pup! Thank you!

I love it here!!! Everyone is great on staff. Dr Whitted is amazing and totally understands my dogs needs even for an annual wellness. We live in the neighborhood & come here for all out vet needs. Highly recommended!

Please don’t take your animals here. I could write a story about how they only made my dogs problems worse but i’ll keep it short. I’ve gone to vets all over the states and never had the bad experiences I did at SCAH. They really messed up when I took my dog to a diffrent place they were amazed at how SCAH had made terrible mistakes in MISDIAGNOSIS and the WRONG MEDICINES!!!  They took my dog in the back all times and told me to wait up front every time my dogs problems only increased. Not to mention making me pay over and over again for the same problems I already paid for. No Compassion
It’s almost like Cheers, but for your pet- they know who they are and what they need. I love this place… and so does my bulldog. She thinks everyone is the bees knees!

It seems this veterinary clinic is not interested in my business...  I called and explained I was looking for a new vet and considering them based upon recommendations.  After a brief hold (I realize a place like this can be busy) I gently asked if I could speak to one of the vets at a time convenient to them.  I was told no, they don't make time for this unless you are an established patient.  I was offered to speak to a staff person but I want to establish rapport with the expert provider, not the assistant.

In my many years as a service provider, I always honored such a request as this so that my team could build a relationship and establish trust.  I would think a small clinic such as this would want to build their client base and get more positive reviews.   I do note that there are no responses to the several very-negative reviews.   In addition, on their website, the "send us an email" button does not work.

Perhaps this is a great clinic but they get a D- grade on marketing and showing an interest in ways to get new clients.   If there is someone monitoring these reviews, I would hope it is either the owner or that they will make the owner aware.

I will check back in a week or so to see if there is any reply to this.

This vet office is wonderful. The front desk staff are kind, and the vet tech Amanda was kind, helpful, and answered all of my (many) questions. They were very supportive and took good care of my pup. Highly recommend!
Not the best. Not the worst.
They are always kind and helpful. Their prices are very high but we can trust the quality of care

I've been taking my dog to Sunset Cliffs Animal Hospital since early 2024, and while my experience started off smoothly, it has completely deteriorated due to their poor communication, rigid policies, and lack of compassion.

I want to be clear--I have pet insurance, I prioritize my dog's health, and I handle situations professionally and level-headedly. I am not someone who avoids necessary vet visits or argues about costs for no reason. But this clinic's unreasonable policies and lack of support made it impossible to trust them with my dog's care.

At first, things went well--I even had a dental cleaning and mass removal done without issue. But after that, red flags started appearing.
First, they failed to disclose that they don't accept CareCredit until after my pet's procedure, leaving me scrambling at checkout.

Then came the excessive charges--I received a notice that my dog needed a booster vaccine, and they charged me a full exam fee for a 10-minute visit without warning. I took responsibility for not asking beforehand, so the next time I made sure to call ahead. After debating with the front desk for 10 minutes, they finally told me I could walk in instead of making an appointment to avoid the charge.

Then came a critical issue: My dog was diagnosed with diabetes in January. Shortly after, I discovered a Vetsulin shortage on the West Coast. I was ahead of the problem and found the medication on Chewy, but SCAH has a policy against calling in or approving online prescriptions. I respected their policy and asked for a written prescription--only to be told I had to wait 48 hours to get it.

When I finally mailed it in, Chewy told me they could accept the prescription over the phone--but SCAH refused to make the call, saying they "don't work with Chewy" even though there were no legal reasons preventing them from doing so. I was left scrambling.

As my dog's insulin ran out, I pleaded for help. Their response? "Call Costco." But Costco was the reason I was in this situation to begin with. Their only other advice? Wait until my dog became lethargic and bring her in then. Essentially, let my dog go into a diabetic coma before they would act.

To make matters worse, they repeatedly failed to follow up on critical lab results. After running tests for both a UTI and her diabetes-related bloodwork, they never called me back--I had to follow up multiple times, waiting nearly two weeks for answers.

Finally, I spoke with the Business Manager, hoping to professionally and calmly voice my concerns. Her response?
1. Their staff "doesn't have the luxury of time" to help beyond the basics.
2. They did "help" by calling other hospitals--except none of those hospitals had the medication.
3. They couldn't call Chewy because if they did it for me, they'd have to do it for everyone.

I asked point-blank: "So you wouldn't even make an exception if my dog was going to die?"

Her answer: "No."

At that point, I knew I had to find another vet. I calmly told the business manager that I thought it was best to move forward with my pet's care elsewhere then - two hours later they sent me an email stating they were "discontinuing services with me"--as if they needed to have the last word. It felt petty and unprofessional.

Leaving a Vet when your dog is in the middle of a health crisis is the last thing I wanted to do, but I gave SCAH plenty of opportunities to close any gaps. I genuinely thought these were just missteps falling through the cracks rather than an intentional lack of care. But after months of repeated issues, it's clear that better care is available elsewhere for both patients and pet parents alike.

A diabetes diagnosis is already overwhelming, but instead of guiding me through it, they made everything significantly harder.

I deeply regret trusting them with my dog's care. If you want a vet that truly supports pet owners and prioritizes patient well-being, go somewhere else.
